first.rationale: The immediate competitive threat is concentrated in price-sensitive SMBs, and inherited evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing improved acquisition and revenue in that segment. I would verify that result and the strongest onboarding alternative before committing, while using a guarded, targeted design because discounting may create longer-term value and pricing-positioning risk.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening and simplifying onboarding for self-serve accounts. This directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and has verified evidence of higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (2.1 days), and improved 30-day retention (+3%), making it the strongest supported path to sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue lift was paired with a 12% 30-day retention decline and was explicitly not sustainable.

final2.rationale: Continue with simplified onboarding rather than react with deeper promotional pricing. The verified discount result produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and was explicitly judged unsuitable for sustainable growth; escalating into a competitor price war would risk worsening downstream customer value. Simplified onboarding is verified to improve completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, and directly addresses the current completion decline while strengthening self-serve account value.
